name: William Yeh
desc:
William Yeh founded CSI Technology Group over thirty years ago to offer superior information technology to law enforcement, judiciary and regulatory government agencies. He has led the operations and strategic direction of his company to realize this vision and has successfully provided fully integrated, multi-jurisdictional information sharing systems for police and fire departments, homeland security, prosecutors and attorneys general offices, judiciary and other criminal justice organizations.

Mr. Yeh has partnered with forensic experts, law enforcement leaders and legal scholars to develop solutions that help these agencies fully utilize and share critical information across horizontal and vertical boundaries at all levels of government. He contributes to law enforcement technology forums and associations and brings the latest advances in technology, data sharing, communication and analysis to his clients.

“Our goal is to make society safer,” he explains, as he continues to guide CSI to be a company that makes a difference in the public safety and judicial communities.

name: Richard Norcross
desc:
Prior to retirement from 25 years in law enforcement and joining CSI, Richard Norcross was the Commander of the Intelligence Services Team for the Camden County Prosecutor’s Office. Commander Norcross joined the Prosecutor’s Office after retiring from his Detective post at the Haddon Heights Police Department due to significant gunshot wounds sustained in the line of duty. Prior to that, he was a police officer with the National Park Boro Police Dept.

During his career, Rich has received numerous medals and commendations for law enforcement actions, including the prestigious New Jersey Gold Medal of Valor as well as the Combat Cross and Wounded in Combat Medal. Commander Norcross is the President of the East Coast Gang Investigator’s Association and has also served as a Policy Board Member & Secretary for the Mid Atlantic Great Lakes Organized Crime Law Enforcement Network (MAGLOCLEN). He is still a Trustee for the Camden County Detectives Association and is one of the founding members of the Police Intelligence Group of South Jersey.

Rich also volunteers to work with law enforcement professionals and their families in the aftermath of tragedies that have resulted in serious injury or death to officers.

name: Andrew Chang
desc:
Before being named as the Chief Operating Officer in July 2019, Mr. Yu-Chen (Andrew) Chang held the Division Administrator position in CSI’s Research & Development (R&D) Division. This Division was organized and built under the direction and management of Mr. Chang. The R&D Division has also been recognized and received numerous awards for its technological innovation. The R&D Team plays a crucial role keeping our products at the forefront of the latest technology. In addition, during Andrew’s leadership, the R&D Team acquired crucial patents for software technology in our targeted markets to maximize and secure the company’s core product value and benefits.

Andrew earned a Master’s Degree in electrical engineering from the University of Pennsylvania and the EMBA certification from National Taiwan University. Since joining CSI Technology Group in 2008, Andrew has consistently focused his career in the field of law enforcement and public safety technology. He has held a number of positions ranging from software engineer, project manager, to Division Administrator. Going forward as the Chief Operating Officer of the company, he will continue to uphold the mission statement of our founder Mr. Yeh, “Our goal is to make society safer”.

name: Christopher Rein
desc:
Chris Rein served as the New Jersey State Chief Technology Officer from 2018 until his retirement from State service in early 2026. He was appointed to this role by Governor Phil Murphy.

Prior to becoming State CTO, Chris was the Deputy Director of the New Jersey Office of Homeland Security’s Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Cell, where he also served as the State’s Deputy Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). His experience spans 44 years in developing, integrating, and managing software systems, as well as leading large, complex information technology initiatives.

Earlier in his career, Chris served as Chief Information Officer for the New Jersey State Police. He also spent approximately 20 years advancing through technical and management roles at the former Bell Atlantic and its technology subsidiary, Bellcore.

Mr. Rein earned his undergraduate degree in Computer Science from Rutgers University and a Master’s degree in Technology Management from Stevens Institute of Technology.

name: Peter Ugalde
desc:
Prior to his retirement and joining CSI Technology Group, Captain Peter Ugalde was a 27 year law enforcement veteran of the Town of Dover Police Department in Dover, New Jersey. Captain Ugalde has served in various positions in the police department from police officer, detective, sergeant, lieutenant and captain. He also served as the executive officer, supervising both investigative and patrol functions of the Town of Dover Police Department. He obtained his Bachelor of Arts degree in Criminal Justice and a Masters Degree in Business Management from the College of Saint Elizabeth in Florham Park, New Jersey.

He is a graduate of the Federal Bureau of Investigations National Academy 238th Class and also a graduate of the State of New Jersey Certified Public Manager Course. He also holds various certifications in network support and administration from the Dover Business College located in Dover, New Jersey. He resides in Randolph, New Jersey with his wife and children.

name: Nathan Noyes
desc:
Prior to his retirement from a 22-year career in law enforcement and joining CSI, Nathan Noyes was the Colonel of the New Hampshire State Police. As Colonel, Nate was responsible for an agency of over 600 sworn and civilian personnel. He served as the Co-Director of the New Hampshire Information & Analysis Center, was responsible for the state’s only forensic laboratory, and oversaw all administrative, investigative, operational, and personnel matters for his entire organization.

Throughout his career, Nate held numerous positions of leadership. As State Police Director, he served as a board member for the Police Standards & Training Council, the New England State Police Information Network, the New England State Police Administrators Compact, and was the Chairman for the New England HIDTA.

Nate obtained his Bachelor’s degree in Political Science and Sociology from Quinnipiac University and his Master’s degree in Public Administration from the University of New Hampshire. He is also a graduate of the 274th Session of the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s National Academy and participated in the 45th Session of their National Executive Institute. Nate lives in New Hampshire with his wife and children.

name: John A. Porter
desc:
Prior to joining the CSI Technology Group, John Porter served a 25-year law enforcement career that included four years in local law enforcement with the Deptford Township (NJ) Police Department and twenty-one years with the Gloucester County (NJ) Prosecutor’s Office where he retired as Chief of County Investigators.

During his career with the Prosecutor’s Office, John was assigned to the Major Crimes and Special Investigations Units before becoming part of the agency’s command staff.

As Chief of County Investigators, he headed the Investigation Division where he oversaw criminal investigations, policy development and implementation, internal affairs investigations, agency accreditation, and managed critical incident scenes as the on-scene supervisor of the Gloucester County SWAT Team. John received his undergraduate degree in Public Administration from Fairleigh Dickinson University and resides in Mantua, New Jersey with his wife and two children.

name: Thomas H. Koundry
desc:
Thomas Koundry joins CSI Technology Group with over thirty years of experience in law enforcement and operations. He has experience in leadership roles, in directing and training of law enforcement and civilian personnel.

Most recently, Thomas Koundry served as Chief of Staff for the Union County Prosecutor’s Office. Prior to that, he attained the rank of Deputy Chief at the East Orange Police Department.

During his tenure at the Union County Prosecutor’s Office, Tom’s duties included financial and asset management, police agency liaison, which included regular interfacing with 26 municipal and state law enforcement agencies, Infoshare and Evidence.com county-wide administrator. Tom also served as Interim Director of Union County Prosecutor’s Forensic Laboratory.

In 2014, Tom took on the lead role in managing a project that integrated UCPO case management, document management and all prosecution functionality into the Infoshare system.

During his 26 years with the East Orange Police Department, Deputy Chief Koundry served in many positions in the police department from police officer, detective, sergeant, lieutenant, captain and inspector. Most notably, as the commander of the Violent Crimes Task force.

Tom also served as a volunteer Emergency Management Coordinator for the Township of Byram, where he lives.

name: Gregory Ferry
desc:
Greg joined the CSI Team following a 25-year career with the New Hampshire State Police where he retired as a Captain-Field Area Commander, overseeing multiple troop barracks as well as the Mobile Enforcement Team (MET), a specialized trained unit of troopers tasked with the enforcement of all threats and all hazards encountered throughout the state.

Greg began his career as an active road trooper, quickly gaining a reputation and skillset in the area of enhanced criminal enforcement while appropriately applying search and seizure laws. Greg was a K-9 handler for 14 years, working dual purpose patrol/narcotics detections dogs, gaining strong collaborative partnerships with his local, county, federal law enforcement partners as well as the State Fusion Center and HIDTA. Additionally, he filled roles as an FTO, patrol sergeant, Assistant Troop Commander and Lieutenant- Troop Commander, prior to his promotion to Captain.

Greg served in the U.S. Army as a Military Police Officer after graduating high school, serving in Europe and in the Middle East. He went on to earn his BA in Criminology from the University of Southern Maine. He has been actively involved with Special Olympics throughout his career. Greg lives in Hooksett, NH with his wife and 3 children.

name: John Emmerson-Bolt
desc:
With over 20 years in the Information Technology field before joining CSI, John Emmerson-Bolt’s diverse technical career has given him experience handling many aspects of software development, implementation and support. As a web developer, John developed and supported websites and software for various businesses.

John also has experience as a business analyst and software engineer, as well as a manager of new business development for several software firms. Well-versed in many IT roles, John brings his comprehensive IT experience to CSI as he supports key CSI projects for the New Jersey Judiciary.

John has implemented and supports the case and document management systems for the Supreme and Appellate courts, including the electronic filing component. He holds a BA degree from the University of East Anglia in Norwich, England.

name: James Parent
desc:
Jim brings over 26 years of law enforcement experience to CSI. Twenty-five years of his extensive career of conducting and managing criminal investigations was spent at the Cumberland County Prosecutor’s Office (CCPO). He retired as Captain of Detectives, the executive officer overseeing all the investigative divisions within the office. A key player in the Major Crimes and Narcotics Units for over 20 years, he worked closely with federal, state and local agencies to solve crimes within the county.

While serving at the CCPO, he managed their InfoShare® Records Management database. His knowledge of using InfoShare® products from a police officer and prosecutor’s office perspective gives him a keen understanding of his users’ needs and goals, as he helps them benefit from using InfoShare® to enhance their workflow and save resources. Jim is a graduate of the FBI National Academy class #236 and is an active member of the New Jersey Chapter of the FBINAA. He received his undergraduate degree in Sociology from Catawba College in Salisbury, North Carolina and makes his home in Millville, New Jersey, with his wife and three kids.

name: John P. Denmark
desc:
Prior to joining CSI Technology Group, Sr. Investigator John P. Denmark retired from the Camden County (NJ) Prosecutor’s Office after a 25-year law enforcement career that included thirteen years with the Prosecutor’s Office in 2012 and twelve years in local and campus law enforcement with the Woodbury (NJ) Police Department and the Rutgers University Police (Camden Division). While serving at the Camden County Prosecutor’s Office, Sr. Investigator Denmark was assigned to the Crime Scene Unit for over eleven years.

In addition to his Crime Scene responsibilities, Denmark established countywide services for analog and digital surveillance videos. In recognition, Sr. Investigator Denmark received numerous awards and commendations for his crime scene work as well as his contributions related to audio and video services. His investigations have resulted in numerous court appearances involving crime scene and video testimony. The technical services initiated by Denmark have been continued after his retirement by the CCPO High Tech Crimes Unit. John received his undergraduate degree in Computer Science in 1995 from Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, Camden Campus. He resides in South Jersey with his wife.

name: Kimberly Mikell Petty
desc:
Kim started her 27-year law enforcement career as a dispatcher for the Phillipsburg Police Department. After two years there, she then went on to serve the Somerset County Prosecutor’s Office (SCPO), first in the Intelligence Unit and then as a systems manager. Kim worked with the prosecutor, attorneys and investigative staff to implement policies and procedures that improved office operations.

She led the training and deployment of InfoShare® modules and saw first- hand how InfoShare® products supported the efficiency and productivity initiatives that she and SCPO management were working to implement. Retiring after serving 25 years with the SCPO, Kim brings her expertise to CSI, and now shares her knowledge and experience with prosecutors’ offices and police departments across New Jersey.

name: Matthew Edwards
desc:
After serving 25 years with the Morristown Police Department, Matt retired as a lieutenant and brought his experience and knowledge of police records management to CSI. His extensive law enforcement background covered work in criminal investigations, legal considerations and emergency response services. He was a records management expert and a technology leader within the police department, spearheading a new database implementation and developing policies, procedures and strategies for records management protocols, the analysis of data retention and securing confidential data.

This first-hand knowledge of records management leadership within a police department provides Matt a keen insight to support his CSI clients’ requirements. He now leads the implementation of many of CSI’s regional and local police records management system deployments.

name: Steven J. LaPorta
desc:
Sergeant Steve LaPorta retired from the Gloucester County Prosecutor’s Office, where one of his assignments was to be the InfoShare® System Administrator. His career spans twenty-five years of law enforcement experience, from crash reconstruction to crime scene investigations and forensics. Serving in the Clayton and the Franklin Township Police Departments, he has experience as a detective, patrol officer, a D.A.R.E. instructor, supervisor and special officer and has been assigned to the New Jersey State Police Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force, the US Secret Service Philadelphia Area Electronic Crimes Task Force and the FBI’s Child Exploitation Task Force, just to name a few. He was also the Logistics Coordinator for the Gloucester County Prosecutor’s Office Swat Team.

Steve continues to serve as a volunteer fire fighter for the Minotola Fire Department, where he lives. Over the years, Steve has shared his vast experiences with others as a presenter, instructor and lecturer. He was also a member of the Gloucester County Prosecutor’s Office Speaker’s Bureau. Steve holds a BA in Public Administration from Fairleigh Dickinson University and Masters in Human Resource Training and Development from Seton Hall. He continues to serve the public safety sector as he calls upon his vast law enforcement experience and InfoShare® expertise to help his clients use CSI products effectively and increase their efficiency on the job.

name: Russell D. Christiana
desc:
Russ Christiana comes to CSI after 16 years of service with the Bergen County Prosecutor’s Office (BCPO), where he was an avid user of InfoShare® products to support his work. During his tenure at the BCPO, he served in the Special Victims Unit, the Recruit Police Training Unit and the Major Crimes Unit. He assisted in over 100 homicide investigations and conducted over 50 crime scene investigations. He was dedicated to serving victims of sex crimes and child abuse cases, working cooperatively with Sexual Assault Nurse Examiner (SANE) professionals and counselors of Rape Crisis, the Division of Youth and Family Services and Victim/Witness Advocates.

He conducted hundreds of interviews of victims, suspects and witnesses, conducted crime scene investigations and testified in numerous high profile homicide and SVU cases in the NJ Superior Court. Through his investigative work, he relied heavily on InfoShare® products, utilizing InfoShare® RMS to record and track his cases and the InfoShare® Major Incident Module (MIM) in complex cases and other high profile investigations. He rose to be the Commanding Officer of all Investigations in the Major Crimes Unit and in the Special Victims Unit. As Russ well knows the value of InfoShare® products to support all types of police and investigative work, he is happy to join our team and help others learn to use these products in their agencies to make their jobs more efficient and effective.

name: Tom Kenny
desc:
With over 25 years in the commercial software industry before joining CSI, for the last 12 years, Tom Kenny worked at a law enforcement records management software provider in Pennsylvania. As a manager in the software provider, Tom has extensive experience in application support, training, product development, sales support and sales. He also has successful history of building and maintaining customer satisfaction and collaborative relationships.

Also, Tom used to play a key role in a small team, which provides software support to over 500 clients via phone and email. Well-versed in many roles, such as customer relations, application support, customer support manager, Tom brings his comprehensive experience to CSI as he supports key CSI projects to customers in Pennsylvania. Tom received his undergraduate degree major in Criminal Justice from LaSalle College, Philadelphia, PA.

name: Jimmy Calderella
desc:
Jimmy joins CSI Technology after more than 24 years with the New Jersey State Police where he served in assignments from road duty, where he proudly spent six years patrolling the New Jersey Turnpike, to eventually being administrator of the NJSP Confidential Source database and all of the Infoshare modules that the NJSP used including the Intelligence Module, iLog Module, and the Major Incident Module (MIM).

During the course of his career he gained experience being in the Casino Operation Unit, and he worked narcotic and street gang investigations with Philadelphia/Camden High Intensity Drug Trafficking Area (PC HIDTA) where he was a monitor room supervisor on numerous wiretaps and used the Infoshare Intelligence Module.

Jimmy’s last assignment was at the Regional Operations Intelligence Center (ROIC), New Jersey’s fusion center, where he was a Detective Sergeant First Class, and Assistant Unit Head of the Information Sharing Unit. While at the ROIC, he was also assigned to various units, including the Intelligence Watch and Warning (IWW) Unit, that fields calls from law enforcement agencies around the world. As the Division's Duty Officer and the State's Watch Officer, he was responsible for monitoring all events that had a nexus to New Jersey.

name: Scott Plumer
desc:
Scott joined the CSI team following a 26-year career in law enforcement retiring as the Patrol Operations Division Commander for the Bedford, New Hampshire Police Department. In his career, he worked as a patrol officer, field training officer, detective, prosecutor, patrol sergeant, and as a lieutenant was the commander of the communications and records division. In his last assignment, he was responsible for leading and managing all police operations, the mountain bike and motorcycle units as well as officers assigned to the Southern New Hampshire Special Operations Unit.

Scott served in the United States Army and was deployed to Operation Joint Guard in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1997-1998. His unit was responsible for public affairs in the headquarters located in Tuzla and Sarajevo. He has been an adjunct faculty instructor since 2009 at Great Bay Community College and since 2019 at Southern New Hampshire University in the Criminal Justice and Homeland Security programs. He has also been a member of the International Association of Approved Basketball Officials since 2003. Scott is also an active member of the New Hampshire Police Association Pipes and Drum as a tenor drummer. He lives in Bedford, NH with his wife Jill.

name: Richard Nilsen
desc:
Prior to his retirement and joining CSI, Richard Nilsen served the citizens of Montgomery County, Pennsylvania for thirty-five years. He most recently served with the Montgomery County District Attorney’s Office where, after serving eleven years in the Homicide Unit, he was promoted to Detective Lieutenant and given command of the agency’s Forensic Services Unit. He was responsible for several major projects, including overhaul of the Detective Bureau’s policy manual, drafting of the Officer Involved Shooting Protocol, and establishment of the Bureau’s Rapid DNA program.

Prior to working with the District Attorney’s Office, Lt. Nilsen served twelve years with the Lower Merion Township Police Department. His assignments included Patrolman, Field Training Officer, Platoon Investigator, SWAT team member, and Detective. During his time with Lower Merion, Lt. Nilsen earned his law degree and was sworn as a Special Assistant District Attorney. He frequently was detached from the police department to work in the District Attorney’s Office.

Lt. Nilsen obtained his undergraduate and graduate degrees from Villanova University and his law degree from Widener University School of Law. He is also a graduate of Northwestern University’s School of Police Staff and Command.

name: Brian D. Womer
desc:
Brian Womer joins the CSI Technology Group team with nearly 40 years in the IT field serving the Technical, Financial, and Government sectors.

Prior to joining CSI, Brian Womer served over 25 years with the New Jersey Department of Law and Public Safety in several capacities, most recently as the Deputy Director of IT. In this role, he led the Project Management and Software Development teams to deploy large scale enterprise solutions for the Department.

Brian has extensive knowledge with projects scaled to meet State Government needs as well as hands on experience with networking, software development, and project management. He has a comprehensive background regarding information and procedures for the handling of Mass Casualty events.

In 2016, Brian was awarded the ‘Solutions Award’ from The Public Safety Technology Institute and the New Jersey Office of Information Technology for his work on the state-wide Alcoholic Beverage Control Licensing System.

name: Paul Genovese
desc:
Paul joins the CSI team following a 32-year career in law enforcement retiring as the Administrative Bureau Commander for the City of Bridgeton Police Department. He has experience in leadership roles, in directing and training law enforcement and civilian personnel, and in police department operations.

During his time at the Bridgeton Police Department, Paul’s duties included implementation and administration of the InfoShare® RMS/CAD systems, development of department policy & procedure, training employees on best practices and protocols, police academy instructor, certified crime analyst, and liaison to the Cumberland County Prosecutor’s Office Intelligence Unit and Entry Team Commander.

Paul will utilize his years of training and experience to assist clients in using CSI’s products effectively and efficiently.

name: Sean Faherty
desc:
Sean joins the CSI Team following a 25-year career in law enforcement with over 23 years with the New Hampshire State Police. While with the New Hampshire State Police, Sean served in multiple Troop barracks and with the State Police Aviation Unit. Sean was an instrumental part of the records management project from the onset. He was an active user with the InfoShare® systems and has significant hands-on experience.

Sean began his career as an active road trooper in northern New Hampshire. After a number of years, he moved to the capital of the State to work within another Troop barracks. After 10 years at that Troop, Sean was transferred into the State Police Aviation Unit. Throughout his career, Sean has fulfilled roles as a Field Training Officer, Drug Recognition Expert Instructor, Emergency Vehicle Operator Course Instructor, Tech Team Lead, HGN/FST Instructor, LIDAR Instructor, Certified Tactical Flight Officer, Stop Stick Instructor, Assistant Project Manager – Records Management and a Body Camera Project Lead. He concluded his career as the Assistant Unit Commander for the State Police Aviation Unit.

Sean also served as a Marine in the United State Marine Corp – Reserves. He is an active professional photographer, living in Concord, NH with his wife and 2 children.

name: Keith McDermott
desc:
Prior to becoming a member of the CSI Team, Keith retired as Captain of the Internal Affairs Bureau after a 29-year career with the Wayne Township New Jersey Police Department.

Keith was a proactive patrol officer, member of the police marine squad and county rapid deployment team and was a first responder to the World Trade Center during the events of 9/11. He was promoted to the rank of Sergeant and supervised staff in multiple bureaus including patrol, investigations, and communications. Before his assignment with Internal Affairs, Keith commanded the communications center as Lieutenant and then the operations division as Captain. Keith managed Wayne Township's public safety CAD and RMS for most of his career.

Keith was a member of the Wayne Township Volunteer Fire Department for 30 years where he attained the rank of Chief and is a founding member of the Passaic County Emerald Society Pipes and Drums. Keith earned his bachelor's degree in marketing from Rutgers University, and lives in New Jersey with his wife and two daughters.

name: Christopher DeHagara
desc:
Chris joins the CSI team after serving 31 years with the East Orange Police Department, ultimately retiring as Lieutenant. He has over 12 years of experience as Narcotics Detective and has taken up numerous roles in law enforcement such as Commander of Criminal Investigations, Supervisor of Information Technology, Supervisor of Strategic Decision Support Center CompStat Unit, and Supervisor of the Evidence Unit.

While with the East Orange Police Department, he was the administrator over several systems, such as InfoShare, AVL, body cameras, and E-ticket. Chris’ expertise in a diverse range of systems allows him to better understand his users' visions and needs to streamline their communication and workflow efficiency.

name: Anthony Sgroi
desc:
Anthony joins our CSI team after dedicating 25 years of his career to the Ridgefield Park Police Department. He began his career in the patrol unit and later transferred to the detective bureau, where he served for nine years, rising to the rank of Sergeant. Afterward, he returned to patrol and commanded a shift until his retirement.

During his tenure with the department, Anthony was the administrator of the InfoShare CAD/RMS/eTicket system and was responsible for training department users on InfoShare applications since its deployment in 2015. He also served as the TAC officer, responsible for training all police department employees. His expertise and professionalism were instrumental in the administration and implementation of all computerized systems for the department. As a Field Training Officer and Dispatcher Training Officer, Anthony ensured all new hires were adequately trained and equipped to serve the community.

Throughout his career with the Ridgefield Park Police Department, Anthony demonstrated a strong commitment to excellence and ensured the department had the tools and technology necessary to protect and serve the community. He brings his vast knowledge of InfoShare applications and user experience to our team and his clients.

name: Nicholas Scerbo
desc:
Nick joins the CSI Team after serving a 27-year career in law enforcement that included one year with the Harrison Police Department and 26 years with the Jersey City Police Department, where he retired as a Deputy Chief of Police assigned to the Office of the Chief.

During his extensive tenure at the Jersey City Police Department, Nick held a range of roles, from his beginnings as a police officer and dispatcher to his progression through detective, sergeant, lieutenant, and captain ranks. His diverse experience equipped him with a multifaceted understanding of law enforcement operations.

He also held pivotal positions in both the patrol and investigations bureaus, such as Major Case Unit Commander, West Detective Commander, Patrol Bureau Tour Commander, Cease Fire Unit Commander, East District Commander, and Executive Officer to the Chief of Police. These roles reflect his strategic thinking, problem-solving skills, and visionary leadership style. In 2019, while a Captain with the JCPD, he was responsible for overseeing the implementation and administration of the InfoShare® RMS/CAD systems.

Nick has taken part in the Police Unity Tour several times. He also served as an executive board member of the Police Superior Officers Association and on their contract negotiating team. Nick obtained his Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting from Rutgers University and lives in North Jersey with his wife and daughter.

name: Adam Hampton
desc:
Adam Hampton joins our CSI team with a distinguished career spanning 25 years at the Hillsdale Police Department in Bergen County, NJ. Beginning as a police dispatcher in 1999, Adam transitioned to a patrol officer role in 2001.

Adam’s extensive background in technology is a cornerstone of his career. He served as the IT manager for the police department, overseeing all hardware, software, and cybersecurity operations. Since 2014, he has been the administrator for InfoShare applications, ensuring the department's technological infrastructure remains cutting-edge and efficient.

Beyond his IT responsibilities, Adam dedicated eleven years to the detective bureau, where he held positions as a School Resource Officer, Detective, and Detective Sergeant. These roles showcased his commitment to community policing and public outreach programs.

Throughout his tenure at the Hillsdale Police Department, Adam remained committed to supporting the needs of the department, the borough, and its residents. His focus on technical innovation and excellence ensured that the department had the tools and technology necessary to effectively protect and serve the community.

Joining our CSI team, Adam brings a wealth of knowledge and experience, particularly with InfoShare applications. His background in technology and community service will complement our team's capabilities and service offerings to enhance user experience and operational efficiency.

name: Robert Barber
desc:
Robert brings a wealth of experience to the CSI team after a distinguished 25-year career in law enforcement. He spent four years with the New Shoreham Police Department and 21 years with the Narragansett Police Department in Rhode Island. Over the course of his career, Robert took on a variety of roles, including dispatcher, patrol officer, investigator, and supervisor in both patrol and detective units. He ultimately retired as the department’s Prosecution Lieutenant. Additionally, Robert served as a firearms instructor, Field Training Officer, and was part of both the Accident Reconstruction Unit and the Warrant Service Team.

He holds a bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice and a master’s certificate in Computer Forensics from Roger Williams University. Robert currently resides in Rhode Island with his wife and daughter.

name: Daniel Sorice
desc:
Daniel joins our CSI team after over 20 years of dedicated service in law enforcement. He began his career as a dispatcher with the Johnston, RI Police Department before moving on to the Narragansett Police Department, where he served in various roles, including patrol officer, detective, sergeant, and lieutenant.

Throughout his career, Daniel also held several specialized positions. He was a Field Training Officer (FTO), a certified instructor in Mental Health First Aid, and BCI Certified. He concluded his law enforcement tenure as the department’s Administrative Lieutenant, where he led the development and management of the Body-Worn Camera program. Additionally, Daniel served as the department’s Accreditation Manager, successfully overseeing two re-accreditations and earning the Rhode Island Accreditation Manager of the Year Award in recognition of his work.

Daniel holds a master’s degree in criminal justice and a master’s certificate in cybersecurity from Roger Williams University. He currently resides in Rhode Island with his wife and children.

name: Edward Flynn
desc:
Ed joins the CSI team after serving over 26 years as a State Trooper with the New Hampshire State Police. Over the course of his career, he spent many years actively patrolling the midnight shift and served as an instructor in Defensive Tactics, Baton, and Taser, training both new recruits and seasoned officers.

Ed was certified as an explosives detection handler and worked with three explosive detection canines throughout his tenure. After completing specialized training with the Bomb Squad, he was selected to become a Bomb Technician, earning numerous certifications and working alongside bomb squads across New England. He played a key role in the growth and advancement of the Bomb Squad, contributing to improvements in equipment, training, personnel, and response capabilities. He retired as the Assistant Bomb Squad Commander after nearly 18 years of service on the team.

Ed brings valuable hands-on experience using the InfoShare® System from his time as a New Hampshire Trooper. He also possesses extensive training in software technologies, with expertise ranging from robotics and x-ray platforms to bomb data reporting software.

name: Sean McCarty
desc:
Sean brings more than two decades of public service experience to his role at CSI, following a 24-year career as a full-time firefighter in his hometown of Belmont, New Hampshire. He retired as a Lieutenant after leading initiatives in fire investigation, recruitment and retention, equipment procurement, and the design and delivery of training programs.

With a deep understanding of fire service operations and the day-to-day challenges they face, Sean leverages his field experience to help agencies identify and implement solutions that improve efficiency and support their mission.

Based in Belmont, Sean remains active in his community, coaching youth baseball and supporting the Belmont Fire Department on an as-needed basis. He values teamwork, clear communication, and a grounded, service-first approach in everything he does.

name: Sara Luckus
desc:
Sara joins the CSI team after a distinguished 31-year career with the Middlesex County Prosecutor’s Office (MCPO) in New Jersey, where she retired as the IT Manager. She began her career in 1994 as an administrative clerk before transferring to the Victim Assistance Unit, where she served as a Victim Advocate.

As technology became increasingly integral to law enforcement operations, Sara returned to school and, upon graduation, joined the MCPO IT team. She advanced quickly, becoming IT Manager in under two years. In this role, she consistently modernized the office’s technological capabilities, ensuring systems remained efficient and secure.

Sara served as the administrator of the InfoShare® RMS and was responsible for training agency personnel and local law enforcement users on the application following its expansion in 2002. She also led system enhancements and implemented new features designed to improve functionality and operational effectiveness across the office.

In addition to her IT leadership, Sara managed numerous administrative projects and responsibilities. She is a graduate of the Certified Public Manager (CPM) program through Fairleigh Dickinson University. Joining CSI, she brings decades of technical expertise, leadership, and hands-on InfoShare® experience to the account management team. She lives in northeast Pennsylvania with her husband, Jason.

name: Norman Galipeau
desc:
Norman joined CSI following a distinguished 34-year career in law enforcement, retiring as a Captain with the Woonsocket, Rhode Island Police Department, where he served as Operations Division Commander. He brings more than 27 years of supervisory leadership experience, with a career spanning operations command, professional standards, accreditation, training, technology modernization, and policy development.

Throughout his tenure, Norman led major organizational initiatives, including the deployment of body-worn cameras, the development of departmental policy manuals, and the integration of key technology platforms. He also served as project lead for Woonsocket Police Department’s implementation of the InfoShare® CAD/RMS system. His command responsibilities included oversight of Professional Standards, Training, Recruiting, Communications, and Evidence functions, along with extensive leadership in investigations and IT management.

Beyond his departmental service, Norman has been a longtime assessor and consultant with the Rhode Island Police Accreditation Commission, assisting agencies statewide in achieving and maintaining accreditation. He is also committed to community engagement, having co-organized Copswalk events in support of families of fallen officers throughout the New England region.

Norman resides in Rhode Island with his wife, Caroline.

name: Dr. Henry Lee
position: Former Commissioner of Public Safety, State of Connecticut
desc:
Dr. Henry C. Lee, former Commissioner and Lab Chief of the Department of Public Safety for the State of Connecticut, is currently a distinguished professor at the University of New Haven, Chief Emeritus of Forensic Science Services of Connecticut, and the Director of the Institute of Forensic Research and Training Center.

Dr. Lee came to national prominence as an expert witness during the O.J. Simpson trial. He has assisted law enforcement agencies throughout the US and abroad on special missions. A graduate of John Jay College of Criminal Justice, Dr. Lee also received a doctorate in biochemistry from New York University.

He has also been awarded honorary doctoral degrees from Bridgeport University, the University of New Haven, St. Joseph's College, and William College Law School. Dr. Lee resides in Branford, Connecticut and his office is located at the University of New Haven. You can contact Dr. Lee at www.henryleeinstitute.com.
